Subset a NICHESObject to a Set of Cells

Source: R/NICHESObject_class.R
sub-.NICHESObject.Rd

Filters all cell-indexed slots ($cell.list, $cell.data, $cell.meta, the three neighborhood slots and every table in $aggregations) to the cells in i, and all edge-indexed slots ($edge.list, $edge.data, $edge.meta) to keep only edges where both sending and receiving cells are in i. If $segmentation is populated, it is filtered to retain only rows whose cell is in the retained set. Slot-level invariants are re-validated by the internal constructor before the subset is returned.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'NICHESObject'
x[i, ...]

Arguments

x

A NICHESObject.

i

Character vector of cell barcodes to retain.

...

Unused. Present for S3 method signature conformance.

Value

A new NICHESObject restricted to the retained cells and their fully-internal edges, with their neighborhood entries and aggregation rows unchanged. Gene and LRM slots are unchanged.

Details

Cell barcodes in i that are not present in x$cell.list are silently dropped. If the intersection is empty the function errors rather than returning an unusable empty object.

Neighborhoods and aggregations after subsetting

A retained cell keeps its neighborhood entries and aggregation rows unchanged, so they still describe its whole neighborhood in the full object, including neighbors outside i. Aggregate the full object first, then subset. Summing a cell's edges in $edge.data can give less than its aggregation row, because the edge slots hold only edges between retained cells; a export_to_TissuePlex export of the subset shows those edges only.

Aggregations cannot be recomputed on a subset whose neighborhoods include removed edges: add_neighborhood_edge_agg and add_neighborhood_composition stop with an error. To analyze the subset as a separate tissue instead, call add_neighborhoods(obj, overwrite = TRUE) first. This rebuilds the neighborhoods from the retained edges and clears the carried-over aggregation tables.

See also

is_NICHESObject to validate the result.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1L)
count.mtx <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
  i = sample(6L, 30L, replace = TRUE),
  j = sample(8L, 30L, replace = TRUE),
  x = as.numeric(rpois(30L, lambda = 3) + 1L),
  dims = c(6L, 8L),
  dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", 1:6), paste0("Cell", 1:8))
)
meta.data <- data.frame(
  x = runif(8L), y = runif(8L),
  row.names = paste0("Cell", 1:8)
)
LRM.db <- data.frame(
  ligand   = c("Gene1", "Gene3"),
  receptor = c("Gene2", "Gene4")
)
obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx = count.mtx, meta.data = meta.data, LRM.db = LRM.db,
  mode = "spatial", ligand.col = "ligand", receptor.col = "receptor",
  k = 3L, n.cores = 1L, verbose = FALSE
)
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 3 | Cells: 8 | Inter-cell: 18 | Autocrine: 8
#> [compute_CellToCell] 26 edges x 2 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 9 non-zero edge signals.

# Subset to the first four cells; only fully-internal edges are kept
sub <- obj[paste0("Cell", 1:4)]
dim(sub)
#> cells genes edges  LRMs 
#>     4     6     6     2 
# }
